chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch 468: Li Huowang’s Hospital Visit and the Egg Custard Lie
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang visits his mother at the psychiatric hospital. He uses lies to comfort her, but his pragmatic coldness reveals a deeper corrosion. A chillingly quiet chapter.
og_title: The Cost of a Smile: Dao Gui Yi Xian Chapter 468
og_description: Li Huowang returns to the hospital for a single meal. The horror isn't monsters—it's his own efficiency.
twitter_title: Ch 468: Li Huowang lies to his mom and it breaks your heart.
twitter_description: He promises her video games, skydiving, and a wedding. Then he goes back to the dark world.

lore_anchors.definition: A classic, soft Chinese steamed egg dish, often given to the ill or elderly as comfort food. Li Huowang’s insistence that he ate this, and not something from the ground, is a fragile assertion of reality.
A loaded term. The Zuowandao (“Way of Sitting in Forgetfulness”) is a cult of liars who twist reality. By using their methods to cheer up his mother, Li Huowang weaponizes his trauma for a kind act.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Li Huowang lie to his mother about playing games and marrying Yang Na?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He uses “small Zuowandao tricks” to redirect her anxiety into a happy fantasy, because he has calculated that spending more time with her would waste time he needs for cultivation.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the significance of the egg custard exchange with Li Sui?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Li Sui saw him eating something from the ground in the Dao-Twisted World, but Li Huowang forcefully corrects her, insisting he ate the hospital meal. This shows him policing the boundary between worlds through sheer verbal authority.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Li Huowang think he feels older than his 18 years?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He speculates that the two-hour time difference between the two worlds might cause his bodies to age at different rates, which briefly opens a new doubt about which world is “real.”
